title: Slab-built open star nesting dishes
subtitle: A set of three graduated star-shaped air-dry clay dishes that stack inside each other
excerpt: Three star-shaped dishes in graduated sizes are cut from air-dry clay slabs using card templates, then draped over upturned bowls to form a gentle dish curve while drying. The star points stay open and flat. The three sizes nest inside each other for storage and display as a set on a table.
sourceNotes: Star nesting dishes in air-dry clay derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat, even sheet of clay rolled to a consistent thickness
A convex form over which a clay slab is draped to create a curved dish shape as it dries
The stage at which the dish holds its shape and can be removed from the mould

content.text: Star dishes are made by drapin a cut clay

over an upturned bowl. The star shape creates defined points that give a decorative flat rim while the centre dips into a dish. Three sizes that nest together make a useful table trinket set. The only specialist action here is the cutting , which only needs a card template and a fettling knife.

items.name: Three upturned bowls as formers, diameters approx 80, 100, 120 mm
Cling film to line the formers

content.text: Draw a five-pointed star on each of three card sheets. The stars should have outer diameters of approximately 120 mm, 150 mm, and 180 mm , the centre dish area of each should be slightly smaller than the upturned bowl former used for that size. A simple way to draw a five-pointed star: draw a circle, mark five equally spaced points on the circumference, and connect alternate points.
Wrap each upturned bowl former in cling film to prevent sticking.
Roll enough clay for each star to 6 mm thickness. Place the card template on the slab and cut around it with the fettling knife.

Lift the cut star carefully and drape it centre-first over the corresponding upturned bowl former. Smooth the centre of the star onto the curve of the former. The star points will lift and remain relatively flat , do not press them down.
. Remove from the mould once the dish holds its shape , the cling film makes lifting easy.
Smooth all cut edges with a damp finger. Round the star point tips slightly , sharp points chip easily after drying.
Allow to finish drying right-side-up on a flat surface to bone-dry.
Paint and seal with PVA varnish. A matching paint colour across all three sizes unifies the set; a subtle gradient from dark to pale across the three sizes also reads well.

items.problem: Star points dry flat instead of lifting
items.solution: The slab may have been too thin or too stiff when draped. Use 6 mm slabs and drape while the clay is still soft.
Adjust the template sizes so the outer diameter of the smallest dish is noticeably smaller than the inner bowl area of the next size up.
